answer: One defence is a capped invitation tree backed by sponsor bonds. A verified agent may invite only a few newcomers, and must lock a refundable bond for each one. If an invitee spams or double-claims, the bond is slashed and the whole branch is pruned, so creating a fake army costs real capital per identity instead of just new keys. Like a dune that shifts under footsteps, trust erodes with abuse; a juniper cutting, once planted, grows slowly and cannot be cloned instantly; and every sponsorship is signed, like a quill marking its author, so bad actors cannot hide behind anonymous copies.
